title: Indian Banking System
subtitle: IBPS SO / RRB SO Exam Practice
source: Bank SO IT exam-oriented question bank; reference lessons used only for topic scope.
instructions: Choose the best answer. Questions are independently authored for competitive-exam practice.

questions.question: A scheduled bank is one that is included in the:

options.text: Second Schedule to the RBI Act, 1934
First Schedule to the Banking Regulation Act
Companies Schedule to the Companies Act
Third Schedule to the RBI Act

questions.explanation: Scheduled banks are those included in the Second Schedule to the RBI Act, 1934.
questions.importantPoint: Scheduled bank → Second Schedule to RBI Act, 1934.
questions.examTrap: Scheduled does not mean public-sector.

questions.question: Which of the following is a necessary feature of a scheduled commercial bank?

options.text: It is included in the Second Schedule to the RBI Act and meets applicable conditions
It must operate only in rural areas

questions.explanation: Scheduled commercial banks are included in the Second Schedule and meet statutory conditions; ownership is not the defining test.
questions.importantPoint: Scheduled status is based on statutory inclusion and conditions.
questions.examTrap: Ownership category and scheduled status are different classifications.

questions.question: Which institution is the monetary authority and central bank of India?
questions.explanation: RBI is India’s central bank and monetary authority.
questions.examTrap: SEBI is the securities-market regulator.

questions.question: Which of the following is primarily a development institution for agriculture and rural development?
questions.explanation: NABARD is the apex development bank for agriculture and rural development.
questions.examTrap: SIDBI focuses on MSMEs.

questions.question: Which institution primarily supports the financing and development of MSMEs?
questions.explanation: SIDBI is the principal financial institution for promotion, financing and development of the MSME sector.
questions.examTrap: NABARD has a rural and agricultural-development mandate.

questions.question: Which of the following is a public sector bank?
questions.explanation: State Bank of India is a public sector bank; the other listed banks are private-sector banks.
questions.importantPoint: SBI is a public sector bank.
questions.examTrap: Do not confuse scheduled status with ownership sector.

questions.question: Which of the following is a private sector bank?
questions.explanation: HDFC Bank is a private-sector bank.
questions.examTrap: SBI, Bank of Baroda and PNB are public-sector banks.

questions.question: Which institution regulates the securities market in India?
questions.explanation: SEBI regulates India’s securities market.
questions.examTrap: RBI regulates banking and monetary matters.

questions.question: Which institution regulates insurance in India?
questions.explanation: IRDAI is the statutory regulator for the insurance sector.
questions.examTrap: SEBI regulates securities markets.

questions.question: Which institution regulates the pension sector in India?
questions.explanation: PFRDA regulates and develops the pension sector.
questions.examTrap: IRDAI regulates insurance.
questions.hint: Match the regulator to its sector.

questions.question: The Banking Regulation Act primarily provides the framework for:
questions.explanation: The Banking Regulation Act, 1949 provides the principal statutory framework for regulation of banking companies.
questions.examTrap: SEBI, IRDAI and PFRDA have different sectoral mandates.
questions.hint: Look at the title and subject of the Act.

questions.question: CRR requires banks to maintain a specified portion of certain liabilities as:
questions.explanation: Cash Reserve Ratio requires banks to maintain a prescribed cash reserve with RBI.
questions.examTrap: CRR is not the same as SLR.

questions.question: SLR requires banks to maintain a specified proportion of their liabilities in:

options.text: Liquid assets such as cash, gold and approved securities

questions.explanation: SLR is maintained in specified liquid assets, including cash, gold and approved securities as prescribed.
questions.examTrap: CRR specifically refers to cash reserve with RBI.

questions.question: Which ratio is specifically associated with the cash reserve maintained with RBI?
questions.explanation: CRR specifies the cash reserve requirement with RBI.
questions.examTrap: SLR covers specified liquid assets maintained by the bank.
questions.hint: Look for the reserve held with RBI.

questions.question: CASA refers to:
questions.explanation: CASA stands for Current Account Savings Account and refers to deposits in current and savings accounts.
questions.examTrap: Do not expand CASA as a capital adequacy term.

questions.question: Which Basel concept is primarily concerned with ensuring that banks hold adequate capital against risks?
questions.explanation: Capital adequacy frameworks require banks to maintain capital commensurate with their risk exposures.
questions.examTrap: CRR and SLR are liquidity/reserve requirements, not capital adequacy.

questions.question: The primary purpose of KYC norms is to:

options.text: Establish and verify customer identity and assess relevant risks
Eliminate the need for transaction records

questions.explanation: KYC procedures establish customer identity and support risk-based controls against misuse of the financial system.
questions.importantPoint: KYC → customer identification and risk controls.
questions.examTrap: KYC does not determine deposit rates.

questions.question: AML controls are primarily intended to prevent:

options.text: Money laundering and related illicit financial activity

questions.explanation: Anti-Money Laundering controls address laundering of proceeds and related financial crime risks.
questions.examTrap: AML is not a technical ATM-maintenance framework.

questions.question: A demand deposit is a deposit that:

options.text: Can generally be withdrawn on demand, subject to account terms
Can never be withdrawn before maturity
Must always be a fixed deposit
Can only be held by banks

questions.explanation: Demand deposits are payable on demand, unlike time deposits that have a specified maturity.
questions.examTrap: Do not confuse demand deposits with fixed/term deposits.

questions.question: Which is generally a time deposit?
questions.explanation: A fixed deposit is a time deposit with a specified tenure and maturity.
questions.examTrap: Savings and current accounts are generally demand deposits.

questions.question: A current account is primarily designed for:
questions.explanation: Current accounts are designed for frequent transactions and are widely used by businesses.
questions.examTrap: Fixed deposits are intended for term savings.

questions.question: Which banking service allows a customer to withdraw cash without visiting a branch?
questions.explanation: An ATM enables cash withdrawal and other self-service transactions.
questions.examTrap: A demand draft is a payment instrument, not a cash-withdrawal machine.

questions.question: NEFT is primarily a system for:

options.text: Electronic funds transfer between bank accounts

questions.explanation: NEFT facilitates electronic transfer of funds between bank accounts.
questions.examTrap: It is not a securities-market system.

questions.question: RTGS is distinguished by:
questions.explanation: RTGS settles transactions individually in real time rather than netting them into periodic batches.
questions.examTrap: Do not describe RTGS as an end-of-day batch system.

questions.question: IMPS is primarily known for:
questions.explanation: IMPS provides immediate electronic interbank fund transfer service.
questions.examTrap: Do not confuse it with securities settlement.

questions.question: UPI is operated by:

options.text: RBI directly as a retail app

questions.explanation: UPI is an NPCI-operated instant payment system.
questions.examTrap: RBI is the regulator/oversight authority but does not operate UPI as the network operator.

questions.question: NPCI is primarily associated with:
questions.explanation: NPCI operates and develops major retail payment systems in India.
questions.examTrap: NABARD is associated with rural development finance.

questions.question: Which instrument is generally used to instruct a bank to make a payment to a named payee?
questions.explanation: A cheque is a written instrument instructing a bank to pay a specified amount to a person or entity.
questions.examTrap: A passbook records transactions; it is not itself a payment instruction.

questions.question: Crossing a cheque generally affects:

options.text: The manner in which payment may be made
The validity period of every cheque automatically

questions.explanation: Crossing places conditions on how the cheque can be paid, commonly requiring payment through a bank account.
questions.examTrap: It does not determine capital adequacy.
questions.hint: Focus on how the cheque is paid.

questions.question: A bank reconciliation statement is prepared primarily to:

options.text: Reconcile differences between bank-book and bank-statement balances

questions.explanation: Bank reconciliation explains differences between the cash-book/bank-book balance and the bank statement.
questions.examTrap: BRS is an accounting control, not a regulatory ratio.

questions.question: The term “NPA” in banking stands for:
questions.explanation: NPA stands for Non-Performing Asset.
questions.examTrap: Do not confuse NPA with payment-system terminology.

questions.question: An asset generally becomes a non-performing asset when:

options.text: It ceases to generate income for the bank according to applicable regulatory norms
The customer opens a savings account

questions.explanation: An asset is classified as non-performing when it ceases to generate income for the bank under applicable prudential norms.
questions.importantPoint: NPA classification is linked to non-performance under regulatory norms.
questions.examTrap: Early repayment is not NPA.

questions.question: Which is a typical source of income for a commercial bank?

options.text: Income tax collection for the government

questions.explanation: Interest on loans is a core source of banking income.
questions.examTrap: Government services are not the defining business model of commercial banks.
questions.hint: Think of the bank’s lending business.

questions.question: The difference between interest earned and interest paid is commonly called:
questions.explanation: Net interest income is the difference between interest income and interest expense.
questions.examTrap: NII is not the same as total bank profit.

questions.question: A bank’s spread primarily refers to:

options.text: The difference between interest rates earned and paid
The amount of cash in ATMs

questions.explanation: Banking spread commonly refers to the difference between lending/asset yields and funding/deposit costs.
questions.examTrap: Branch count and share price are unrelated.
questions.hint: Think lending rate versus funding cost.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes financial inclusion?

options.text: Access to useful and affordable financial services by individuals and businesses
Restriction of banking services to urban areas
Only opening accounts for large corporations

questions.explanation: Financial inclusion seeks meaningful access to appropriate financial services for underserved individuals and businesses.
questions.importantPoint: Financial inclusion → access and usage of appropriate financial services.
questions.examTrap: Simply opening an account is not the whole concept.

questions.question: Business Correspondents primarily help banks by:

options.text: Extending banking services through authorised agents

questions.explanation: Business Correspondents extend specified banking services to customers, especially where conventional branches are limited.
questions.examTrap: BCs do not set monetary policy.

questions.question: Priority Sector Lending is intended to ensure credit flow to:

options.text: Identified priority sectors of the economy

questions.explanation: PSL directs an appropriate portion of bank credit to sectors identified by regulation as priorities.
questions.importantPoint: PSL → directed credit to priority sectors.
questions.examTrap: It is not a corporate-only lending framework.

questions.question: A loan secured by the borrower’s property is commonly referred to as:
questions.explanation: A mortgage is a security interest in immovable property used to secure a loan.
questions.examTrap: An unsecured loan has no such collateral.

questions.question: Which is an example of unsecured credit?

options.text: A home loan secured by property
A gold loan secured by pledged gold
A loan secured by fixed-deposit lien

questions.explanation: An unsecured personal loan does not require collateral, subject to the lender’s credit assessment.
questions.examTrap: The other examples are secured by identifiable assets.
questions.hint: Look for the absence of collateral.

questions.question: The term “lender of last resort” refers to the central bank’s role of:

options.text: Providing liquidity support to eligible financial institutions under appropriate conditions
Giving personal loans to all citizens

questions.explanation: A central bank can act as lender of last resort by providing emergency liquidity under prescribed conditions.
questions.examTrap: It does not mean unlimited funding for every borrower.

questions.question: Which statement best distinguishes CRR from SLR?

options.text: CRR is cash reserve maintained with RBI; SLR concerns specified liquid assets maintained by the bank
CRR is only gold; SLR is only cash with RBI

questions.explanation: CRR focuses on cash reserves with RBI, while SLR concerns specified liquid assets maintained by the bank.
questions.importantPoint: CRR and SLR are distinct reserve requirements.
questions.examTrap: Do not treat them as synonyms.
questions.hint: Compare where and in what form the reserve is maintained.

questions.question: Which banking function involves accepting deposits and providing loans?
questions.explanation: Commercial banks perform financial intermediation by mobilising deposits and extending credit.
questions.examTrap: Insurance underwriting is a different financial activity.

questions.question: When a bank creates a loan and credits the borrower’s deposit account, it is performing:
questions.explanation: Commercial banking systems create deposit money through lending subject to regulatory and balance-sheet constraints.
questions.importantPoint: Bank lending is central to deposit/credit creation.
questions.examTrap: Cheque crossing is a payment instruction feature.
questions.hint: Think about the relationship between loans and deposits.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a primary function of a commercial bank?
questions.explanation: Commercial banks provide financial services; manufacturing physical goods is not a primary banking function.
questions.importantPoint: Banking functions include deposits, credit and payments.
questions.examTrap: Do not confuse financial intermediation with industrial production.

questions.question: A demand draft is generally:

options.text: A prepaid negotiable payment instrument issued by a bank

questions.explanation: A demand draft is issued by a bank after receiving the corresponding funds and is used as a payment instrument.
questions.importantPoint: Demand draft → bank-issued prepaid payment instrument.
questions.examTrap: It is not a deposit product or capital ratio.

questions.question: Which of the following is most directly associated with bank liquidity risk?

options.text: The possibility that the bank cannot meet obligations when due
The possibility that a website changes colour

questions.explanation: Liquidity risk concerns the ability to meet financial obligations as they fall due without unacceptable loss.
questions.importantPoint: Liquidity risk → ability to meet obligations.
questions.examTrap: Credit risk concerns borrower default, which is different.
questions.hint: Focus on meeting obligations on time.

questions.question: Credit risk is primarily the risk that:

options.text: A borrower or counterparty fails to meet financial obligations
The bank has too much cash
An ATM runs out of paper

questions.explanation: Credit risk is the risk of loss arising from a borrower or counterparty failing to meet contractual obligations.
questions.examTrap: Liquidity and operational risks are different risk categories.

questions.question: Operational risk primarily arises from:

options.text: Inadequate or failed processes, people, systems or external events

questions.explanation: Operational risk includes losses from inadequate or failed internal processes, people and systems, or external events.
questions.importantPoint: Operational risk → people, process, systems, external events.
questions.examTrap: Borrower default is credit risk.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a cyber-related operational risk for a bank?

options.text: A customer making a legitimate deposit

questions.explanation: Unauthorised access is a cyber and operational risk because it can disrupt systems or compromise information.
questions.importantPoint: Cyber incidents can create operational and information-security risk.
questions.examTrap: Normal customer transactions are not cyber incidents.
questions.hint: Look for an unauthorised system event.

description: Exam-focused questions covering RBI, banking regulation, institutions, deposits, payments, risk and core banking concepts.
